sample.task:
(As I sat there in my room, I began to work on a drawing of my fellow club members as dragons - A Sentinel, a Deathgripper, a Night Fury, a Timberjack, and a Red Death. That’s when I heard someone - it was my “dad”. Of course, he isn’t really my dad - I just call him that. His real name is Masao.)

Masao: “Natsuki, can I talk with you for a moment?”

(I quickly ran downstairs, ignoring the fact my Stormcutter tail is still visible.)

Natsuki: “Sure, what’s up?”

Masao: “I just wanted to check on how you’re doing. I know school and the club have been keeping you busy, and I want to make sure you’re taking care of yourself.”

Natsuki: “Oh, yeah, I’m doing okay. Thanks for checking in.”

Masao: “Good to hear. And I have to say, that drawing you’re working on is looking really impressive. You’re really talented.”

Natsuki: “Thanks, Masao. I’m trying my best.”

Masao: “Well, keep it up. And if you ever need to talk or if anything is bothering you, don’t hesitate to come to me.”

Natsuki: “I will. Thanks for being there for me, Masao.”

Masao: “Of course, Natsuki. You’re like family to me.”

(I smiled at Masao’s words, grateful for the support system I had in my life. As I turned back to my drawing, I felt a renewed sense of inspiration and motivation to keep creating and pursuing my passions. And as I finally finished the drawing, I suddenly got a phone call - it was from Monika. But something was wrong - she was crying. I could also hear two of the others on her end of the phone - Himari was going through her stuff, while Kohana was comforting Monika.)
sample.chosen:
Natsuki: “Monika, what’s wrong? Why are you crying?”

Monika: *sniffles* “I... I found something in my room. Something that... that shouldn’t be there.”

Natsuki: “What is it? Can you tell me?”

Himari: “It’s a letter. A letter from someone who claims to be your real father.”

Natsuki: *gasps* “What?! But... but how?”

Kohana: “We don’t know, Monika. But we’re here for you. We’ll figure this out together.”

Natsuki: “Yes, we will. Monika, we’re your friends. We’ll support you no matter what.”

Monika: *sniffles* “Thank you, guys. I don’t know what I’d do without you.”

Natsuki: “We’ll get through this. And Masao, can you come over? We need your help.”

Masao: “Of course, Natsuki. I’ll be right there.”

(As Masao arrived, the group gathered around Monika, ready to face whatever challenges lay ahead. Together, they would uncover the truth and support each other through the journey.)
sample.rejected:
A chill ran down my spine despite the warmth of the room. Monika crying? That wasn't right. Something was terribly wrong.

"Monika? What's happening?" I asked, my voice tight with worry. The playful lilt I usually used was gone, replaced by a sharp edge of concern.

"Natsuki... it's Sayori," Monika choked out, her voice thick with sobs. "She... she's gone."

The world seemed to tilt on its axis. Sayori? Gone? It couldn't be. Just yesterday we were laughing together at club, her bubbly energy filling the room.

"What do you mean gone?" I demanded, my voice rising in panic. "Where is she?"

"She... she took her own life, Natsuki," Himari's voice, usually so cheerful, was barely a whisper.

Kohana's muffled sobs echoed in the background, adding to the suffocating weight of despair.

My grip tightened on the phone, my knuckles turning white. My mind refused to accept it. Sayori, with her infectious smile and boundless optimism, gone? It was impossible.

"No," I whispered, the word catching in my throat. "This can't be true."

But deep down, a cold, hard truth was settling in. Sayori was gone. And the world, already tinged with the fantastical hues of dragons and magic, suddenly felt unbearably bleak.
